reading.rtitle: Residential Lease Agreement -- Summary of Terms
paras: THE AGREEMENT. This lease is for a furnished one-bedroom apartment and runs for twelve months from the first of July. Rent is due on the first of each month. The due date is the fifth: any payment arriving after the fifth carries a late fee of seventy-five dollars.

WHAT YOU PAY BEFORE YOU MOVE IN. An application fee of fifty dollars, which is not refundable and is charged whether or not the application is approved. A security deposit of one month, which is refundable within thirty days of moving out, less the cost of any damage beyond normal wear. The first month of rent in advance.

UTILITIES. Utilities are not included in the rent. Electricity, gas, water and internet are set up by the tenant, in the tenant's own name, before the move-in date. The landlord is not responsible for delays in installation. Tenants report that internet is the service that takes longest, and it is rarely up and running on the first day.

APPLICANTS WITHOUT A CREDIT HISTORY. Applicants who have recently arrived in the country and have no credit score may still be approved, with either a guarantor who has a United States credit history, or two additional months of rent paid in advance. Employment documentation from the sponsoring institution is accepted in place of a credit report.
reading.source: Teaching lease written for this lesson in the format American residential agreements use. The clauses and the vocabulary are the target; it is not a real contract and must not be relied on for any tenancy.

I am going to set up a bank account this week.

listenings.text: So, the process. It is the same for everybody except in one respect, and that one respect is usually the problem for somebody who has just landed. You will not have a credit score. Not a bad one, none at all, which the system finds harder to read than a bad one. There are two ways round it and both are normal, we do this every month. Either you bring a guarantor who has a United States credit history, or you pay two or three months up front. Your employment documentation from the hospital counts for a lot here, so bring the letter. Now, the money. Three payments before you get the keys. The application fee, fifty dollars, and I want to be very clear that this one does not come back, whether we approve you or not. The security deposit, one month, and that does come back, within thirty days of moving out, minus anything broken. And the first month of rent. And then utilities, which are not included and which people always forget. Electricity, gas, water, internet, all set up by you, in your name, before you move in. The internet is the one that takes longest. Start that call the day you sign, not the day you move.

I had prepared for the exams for two years. I had prepared for the hospital. Nobody had told me to prepare for the paperwork, and the paperwork was the part that nearly broke me. Here is what happened in my first ten days, and it sounds like a joke. The bank wanted a proof of address before it would open the account. The landlord wanted a bank account before he would give me the lease, which is the address. And the phone company wanted both of them before it would give me a number, which the bank had asked for on the form. Three offices, three requirements, and each one was the answer to another one. I sat in a parking lot and laughed, and then I did not laugh. What broke it, in the end, was the letter from the hospital. The employment letter counts, and I did not know it counted, and nobody at any of the three offices volunteered that until I was on my fourth visit. So if somebody arrives next month and asks me, I say two things. Do the bank account first, on the first weekday, before anything else. And write down the name of every single person you speak to, because the next person will tell you something different and you will need to say who told you what.
